findings.title: main()'s own docstring is now false for a ConfigError, and no test covers the new branch
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:116-125 (module docstring for `main`, untouched by this diff)
findings.before: "An exception escaping a verb is printed with its backtrace to `stderr` and returns 3, so a crash is never read as a finding" (main()'s docstring, unchanged by this diff) — and every verb's ConfigError, if not caught locally, hit only the generic branch below and returned 3.
findings.after: `err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)` is now checked FIRST: a ConfigError escaping any of the ~21 verbs that do not catch it themselves is printed WITHOUT a backtrace and returns 2, not 3 — exactly contradicting the docstring's own "an exception escaping a verb ... returns 3" one paragraph above the new code.
findings.why_it_matters: A concrete input that was previously valid to trigger: run any verb other than `config`, `doctor` or a `design *` verb (e.g. `gbg round bank`, `gbg preflight ...`) against a hand-edited `.gbg/config.toml` with a bad key. Before this diff that verb crashed with a backtrace and exit 3; after it, the same input now exits 2 with a one-line message and no backtrace. That is the right fix (the PR's own comment says so, and it is real: only cmd_config, a Doctor check and Design.design_verb caught ConfigError themselves before), but `main`'s docstring — the one place a reader learns the CLI's own exit-code contract — was left asserting the old, now-false blanket claim, and no test in test/ (grepped for ConfigError/backtrace/"crashed —" near Main) exercises the new branch to pin the exit code or the message shape.
findings.description: The diff correctly centralizes ConfigError handling so a hand-edited bad config.toml reads as exit 2 ("cannot evaluate") instead of exit 3 ("crash") on every verb, not just the three that already special-cased it — a real and narrowly-scoped fix, and it does not collide with the three verbs that already catch-and-return-2 themselves (they never rethrow, so the outer branch never double-handles them). But the change is left half-finished: `main`'s own docstring still states unconditionally that "an exception escaping a verb is printed with its backtrace ... and returns 3", which the new branch now falsifies for the whole ConfigError class, and nothing in test/ pins the new exit-2-no-backtrace path. For a package whose entire discipline is that a docstring is the contract and every behaviour change gets a test, shipping the behaviour change without touching either is exactly the kind of gap this instrument exists to catch.
findings.evidence: Docstring (src/CLI/Main.jl, unchanged): "An exception escaping a verb is printed with its backtrace to `stderr` and returns 3, so a crash is never read as a finding". New code immediately below it: "err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)". `grep -rn "ConfigError\|backtrace" test/*.jl` finds no reference to Main's new branch.
